---
title: Keyword search with BM25
lang: en
free: true
---
BM25 (Best Match 25) is the industry-standard lexical ranking function used by search engines such as Elasticsearch and Apache Solr. It scores documents based on the presence and frequency of exact query terms, making it fast and highly predictable for keyword-driven queries.

## Term Frequency and IDF

BM25 builds on TF-IDF but adds two saturation parameters, k1 and b, that control how much weight repeated term occurrences carry and how strongly document length is penalized. A term appearing ten times in a document does not score ten times higher than one appearing once — diminishing returns kick in. Inverse document frequency (IDF) down-weights terms that appear in many documents (stopwords, common adjectives) and up-weights rare, discriminating terms.

## Lexical Matching

Because BM25 operates on a token-level inverted index, it excels when the user types the exact word that appears in the document. It handles typos poorly without a separate spelling-correction layer, and it cannot infer synonyms or paraphrases. Queries like "automobile" will miss documents that only contain "car". This limitation is why lexical retrieval is often combined with semantic (embedding-based) retrieval in modern hybrid pipelines, with scores merged via reciprocal rank fusion.
